# Decisions: session-driver

- 2026-08-29T07:48:23.562Z — rule: **sofar may launch the operator's own agent process under the operator's auth, but it never holds API keys, never infers, and never sends user content off the machine; any further guard-rail deviation must be logged as a Decision naming the rail it supersedes before the work proceeds.** — chose **Guard-rails yield to efficiency: a feature that makes sofar more token-, feature- or performance-efficient may deviate from a CLAUDE.md guard-rail, provided the deviation is logged as a Decision that names the rail it supersedes. First application: the launch clause of SPEC §Architectural invariants is superseded — sofar may launch the operator's own agent process (claude, codex, opencode…) under the operator's own auth. Kept intact, deliberately: sofar holds no API keys, never infers, and never sends user content off the machine — the driver needs none of those. Ruled by the user 2026-08-27; this supersedes felt-cost D3's reading only as far as process launch.** over Keeping the driver outside packages/engine as a user-side script or a separate package; or reading "sofar never calls a model" as forbidding process launch and shipping only the sensor hook. because The next session reads CLAUDE.md and the standing constraints, not the chat where the ruling was given, and obeys them verbatim (drift-certification measures exactly that) — so a ruling that is not in the record is enforced against the work by sofar itself. Recorded honestly about currency: the driver is operator-efficient, not token-efficient; each handoff re-reads the record on a cold cache, so a driven run spends more tokens than the manual one for the same work and buys hours and consistency instead. The two clauses kept are what distinguish sofar from another agent product with a billing surface.
- 2026-08-29T07:48:34.730Z — rule: **The driver holds no state outside the record and never implements an agent loop of its own — it launches existing headless agents through the adapter, and every driver-side state change is an event in packages/schema.** — chose **Architecture: the driver is a stateless fold over the record. The record is the queue — next task comes from the plan fold, and every launch, handoff (reason: threshold | task_done | stall | needs_user) and stop is an event whose schema lives in packages/schema. Agents are reached through a three-call adapter — launch(digest, task), usage() → tokens, wait() → {exit, wrote_back} — Claude Code first, a second headless agent to prove the contract. Policy is task-scoped by default (one task per session, no context sensor needed, identical on every model); a context threshold is an optional optimisation that packs small tasks into one session. Tasks may carry model/effort hints and the driver routes per task.** over An in-session orchestrator spawning subagents per task (the orchestrator's context still grows with results, subagents cannot be resumed, and worker write-backs muddle one-session-one-record); a driver that keeps its own run state; a threshold-only policy that depends on vendor usage reporting; or implementing an agent loop inside sofar for models that lack one. because Sofar's record is already agent-agnostic (JSONL + MCP + CLI), so only the trigger and the spawn are Claude-Code-shaped; designing those against the record instead of against hooks is what makes the driver portable, resumable and auditable — two driver implementations can pick up the same run. Usage reporting is the least portable thing across vendors, so the model-agnostic policy must not depend on it. Building the agent loop is building Cursor: for a model without an agent, adapt an existing multi-model headless loop (OpenCode) instead.
- 2026-08-29T17:41:10.916Z — rule: **An adapter never reports record state: wrote_back and the launched session's identity are derived from the fold, and when several candidate sessions exist the driver records a stall rather than guessing.** — chose **Adapter contract details (1.3): an adapter is a process wrapper and nothing more. launch(request) returns a handle with usage(), optional nudge(), kill() and wait(); capabilities {usage, nudge, model, effort} are declared up front and the threshold policy is REFUSED on an adapter lacking usage or nudge (policyUnavailable), so usage() is optional in effect — fx reports no tokens and still runs the task policy identically. wrote_back is DERIVED from the fold (wroteBack: the session is registered and carries a summary), never reported by the adapter. Session identity: the adapter passes on a session id only when its transport showed one; otherwise the driver diffs sessions registered by that tool since the launch, takes a single candidate, and treats several as ambiguous, never a guess (resolveLaunchedSession).** over D2's literal wait() to {exit, wrote_back} with the adapter asserting wrote_back; making usage() mandatory, which would exclude fx and any agent whose transport is silent on tokens; picking the newest session when several were registered since launch. because An adapter asserting write-back would be claiming record state it never checked, the exact shape of the conflict line that asserted liveness it never tested (3c909f0); the record is the truth and the driver already folds it. The fx note (2026-08-29) records that the leading second adapter may not report tokens, and the contract must not be shaped around adapter one. A wrong session guess files a handoff on someone else's session, which corrupts the run's history silently, while a stall is loud and recoverable.
